newsitem.title: CHINA: China mulls ending loan quotas for big state banks.
newsitem.headline: China mulls ending loan quotas for big state banks.

text.p: China's central bank is considering phasing out the quotas for credit and loans which are a key part of the government's control mechanism for the economy, bankers and analysts said on Thursday.
The quotas are one of the pillars of the centrally-planned economy, under which the Beijing leadership controls nationwide money supply by setting loan limits for major banks.
"We are considering such a move (to abolish the quotas) but no timetable has been set," said a central bank official reached by telephone from Beijing. Other officials declined to comment.
Local media reports have said the People's Bank of China would like to start phasing out the loan quota system from early next year.
The quotas limit loans by the four major state banks, the Construction Bank, Bank of China, the Industrial and Commercial Bank (ICBC) and the Agricultural Bank, to control nationwide money supply.
Banking analysts said the issue had become more significant with the sharp fall in the market share of the Big Four in the past few years.

The four are estimated to handle about 50 percent of all loans in China, compared with more than 80 percent in the late 1980s, with the remainder covered by smaller state banks which are not subject to quota restrictions.
"The abolition of the quota system is a must to turn the major state banks into real commercial banks in line with international practice," said a Beijing-based ICBC banker.

"We believe changes will happen before too long because China's financial reforms are now in full swing," he added. "It is becoming more and more difficult for the central bank to control money supply through the quota system."

The official Economic Information News on Wednesday quoted unnamed officials as saying the central bank would start cancelling quotas for the state banks from as early as next year to accelerate their transformation into commercial banks.

The paper said the central bank has already started ending the quotas on an experimental basis for some banks, such as those in Shanghai, and allowing them to lend purely on the basis of their reserves and debt-to-equity ratio.
Most of Shanghai branches of the major state banks declined to comment, but a spokeswoman for the Shanghai branch of the Bank of China said it had not used the new system.

Since the start of this year, Beijing has started to use other methods to adjust money supply including the establishment of a local currency interbank market early this year and the launch of central bank open market operations in April.
But these methods are still officially in a test phase and their scale is limited by the central authorities.
Analysts said they believed it will be years before the interbank market and open market operations alone will be an effective means of controlling money supply.
